title: Configuring nudgePaymentToken without nudgeSize still triggers up-front equality guard, breaking same-token batches
description: The feature is documented as disabled when EITHER `nudgeSize == 0` or `nudgePaymentToken == address(0)`. The up-front guard, however, only checks the token side. If the owner sets `nudgePaymentToken` first (intending to enable later by also setting `nudgeSize`) but leaves `nudgeSize == 0`, the contract still reverts on any call with `paymentToken == nudgePaymentToken` even though no nudge would be paid. This couples two independently-controlled knobs and creates a surprising deployment ordering hazard.
exploit_scenario: 1) Owner deploys, plans to enable nudge in two steps: first call `setNudgePaymentToken(USDC)`, then later `setNudgeSize(100)`. 2) Between the two transactions, all batches that pay in USDC revert with `BatchMint__NudgeTokenMatchesPaymentToken` even though the feature is effectively disabled (`nudgeSize == 0`).
recommended_mitigation: Tighten the guard to `(_nudgeTokenEntry != address(0) && nudgeSize != 0 && _nudgeTokenEntry == address(paymentToken))`. This makes the guard track the feature's actual enabled state. Alternatively, change `setNudgePaymentToken` to require `nudgeSize != 0` so the two knobs cannot get into the partially-configured state.
notes: Operational hazard rather than security risk. Demoted to QA/low.
